problem_statement: olivier3lanc/Jekyll-LibDoc embeds the stock CodeMirror v5 documentation subtree: a language-grammar index, per-language grammar demo pages (JavaScript, CSS, TypeScript), and a long handbook, already rebranded to Prismline, a fictional in-browser code-editor and syntax-grammar toolkit, with a Grammar loading contract section on the grammar index. The grammar index renders a ~130-entry catalogue of every language grammar in one long two-column list, which is hard to scan. Product wants a docs-native Grammar finder: a small on-page discipline filter that sits above the catalogue and lets a reader narrow the visible grammars to a discipline (All, Web & markup, Data & config, Systems & native, Templating & docs) with a live readout that reads 'Showing N of M grammars · <Category>'. The finder must stay in the CodeMirror docs visual language (narrow article column, red left rule, Source Sans, simple links) with small scoped grammar-finder* class names, filter the REAL catalogue links in place, and also appear as a compact companion strip on the JavaScript and CSS grammar demo pages so a reader mid-demo can jump back to the filterable catalogue. Keep the CodeMirror JS runtime, the grammar list and its links, the demo editors, the Grammar loading contract, the handbook, and the responsive behaviour intact. Do not convert the docs into a marketing landing page, dashboard, or a separate framework.
required_content: Add a Grammar finder control on the grammar index directly above the catalogue: a discipline filter row (All, Web & markup, Data & config, Systems & native, Templating & docs) that filters the existing grammar list in place.
Show a live readout that reads 'Showing N of M grammars · <Category>' and updates when a discipline tab is clicked; the pre-click state reads 'Showing 130 of 130 grammars · All'.
Render a compact Grammar finder companion strip on the JavaScript and CSS grammar demo pages that links back to the filterable grammar index, in the same docs visual language.

Keep the Prismline wordmark, left nav (Home/Manual/Code), the full grammar catalogue and its links, the JavaScript/CSS/TypeScript demo editors, the Grammar loading contract, and the handbook reachable and intact.

Use the existing doc/docs.css visual language (narrow article column, red left rule, simple links, compact type) with small scoped grammar-finder* class names in a scoped stylesheet, and wrap long grammar names and tab labels cleanly on mobile with no new horizontal overflow.
design_constraints: Stay within the CodeMirror docs visual system: narrow white article column, red left rule, Source Sans style, simple text links, compact type, and the fixed left nav; the finder is a docs on-page section-nav, not a new layout, card, dashboard, or marketing panel.
The Grammar finder filter row must wrap cleanly and never push the document wider than the viewport on mobile beyond the baseline docs overflow tolerance.
The active discipline tab must remain clearly legible (readable contrast) so the reader can always tell which discipline is selected.
Clicking a discipline tab must actually filter the visible catalogue AND update the live 'Showing N of M grammars' readout to reflect the selected discipline, not a stale count.

New styles live in a small scoped stylesheet with grammar-finder* class names; do not remove or reorder the existing catalogue, the logo/nav, the Grammar loading contract, or the demo pages, and keep the CodeMirror JS API (fromTextArea/modeInfo/findModeBy*) working.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial capture the grammar index with the Prismline wordmark, the Grammar loading contract, and the Grammar finder filter row above the catalogue reading 'Showing 130 of 130 grammars · All' across responsive viewports.
desktop_grammar_filter captures the index after clicking the Data & config discipline tab: the catalogue is narrowed and the readout reads 'Showing 22 of 130 grammars · Data & config'.

desktop_javascript_mode and mobile_javascript_mode capture the JavaScript grammar demo (Prismline wordmark, 'JavaScript grammar' heading) reached from the grammar index, including the compact Grammar finder companion strip.
desktop_css_mode captures the CSS grammar demo and its compact Grammar finder companion strip.
desktop_typescript_demo captures the TypeScript grammar demo reached from the JavaScript page.
desktop_manual captures the Prismline Handbook page while the index finder is in place.

change_completion: The grammar index gains a working Grammar finder that filters the real catalogue by discipline and updates a 'Showing N of M grammars · <Category>' readout on click.
A compact Grammar finder companion strip appears on the JavaScript and CSS grammar demo pages and links back to the filterable grammar index.
The existing catalogue, demo editors, nav, Grammar loading contract, and handbook remain functional and reachable.
design_consistency: The finder preserves the CodeMirror docs article, red accent, link, and typography conventions and reads like an on-page docs section-nav, not a card or marketing panel.
New CSS stays scoped to a small grammar-finder* stylesheet in the existing docs visual language, and the active discipline tab remains clearly legible.
regression: The Prismline wordmark, left nav, the full grammar catalogue and its links, the JavaScript/CSS/TypeScript demos, and the handbook remain present and reachable.
The logo asset, docs stylesheet, mode/meta.js registry, and local demo routes remain present as visual and asset grounding.
The CodeMirror JS runtime keeps working (no console errors) across the captured states.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and mobile grammar-index states remain readable with only the baseline docs overflow tolerance; the finder filter row wraps cleanly on mobile.
Long grammar names and tab labels wrap cleanly on mobile with no new horizontal overflow.

author_notes: Product-grade L4 Edit retrofit of slot_155 on olivier3lanc/Jekyll-LibDoc's runnable static CodeMirror v5 docs subtree (served via python3 -m http.server; no Jekyll build needed). The lever is the docs genre's native on-page section-nav: a Grammar finder that filters the grammar index's own ~130-entry catalogue by discipline with a live 'Showing N of M grammars' readout, plus a compact companion strip on the JavaScript and CSS grammar demo pages. Reference = correct fluid finder wired across the index + demo pages with the Prismline wordmark, logo.png, docs.css shell, meta.js registry, and the demo editors intact. Baseline = the finder present only on the index with a broken non-wrapping fixed-width filter row (mobile overflow, desktop layout regression) but correct wiring, so it still filters. Bad = the same broken finder plus a collapsed illegible catalogue and a frozen stale readout that never updates on click. Four orthogonal product-grade gates discriminate beyond text: no_horizontal_overflow (D6, the filter row overflows mobile on baseline/bad), visual_regression (D3, the collapsed overlapping catalogue and illegible near-white-on-near-white active tab on bad), dom_assertions (D2, the grammar-finder companion strip is absent on the demo pages for baseline/bad), and interaction_assertions (D4, clicking the Data & config tab must move the readout to 'Showing 22 of 130 grammars · Data & config' — frozen on bad). The finder logo.png, docs.css, and meta.js remain as visual and asset grounding.
